triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: The +25% UK section 232 consolidated rate under HTS 9903.82.04 was encoded as starting 2026-07-23 when the Rev12 consolidation took effect 2026-07-21, leaving entries on 07-21 and 07-22 without the UK overlay.
triage.triage_notes: Same pattern as index 1 (single-rule parameter module, one effective_from line, formula 0.25 unchanged). Corpus row us/statute/hts/9903.82.04 confirms the +25% UK rate but carries no effective date, so the 07-21 date rests on the commit message. Companion test unchanged; manifest re-signed with manual_exception "repair".
triage.verifier_justification: The entire module diff is the version-window start of the sole parameter rule moving from '2026-07-23' to '2026-07-21', with the formula (0.25), scope, proof atoms, excerpt, and citation path unchanged, so it is a meaning change and not provenance bookkeeping. The commit message names exactly this repair ("Rev12 section-232 consolidations effective 2026-07-21 (was 07-23)") as a cross-review finding, and the sibling non-UK module (9903.82.02) got the identical 07-23 to 07-21 correction in the same commit, which is what an encoded effective date disagreeing with the revision's real effective date looks like. The PR body corroborates that 2026-07-23 was a lane-wide default rather than a source-derived date: it admits "heading modules carry effective_from 2026-07-23" while the forced-labor component was gated at 2026-07-24, and 07-23 is also the composition window boundary. I tried to refute this as mechanical or as new coverage and could not: an effective_from edit is explicitly a version-window change, and nothing was added to the module.
triage.verifier_notes: Two caveats for the reviewer, neither of which changes the kind. (1) Source grounding is indirect: resolving us/statute/hts/9903.82.04 through the pinned release (us-rulespec-2026-08-03-ecps-pit-tariff-union, provision sha 2e85fba6...) returns only "Articles of aluminum or of steel and derivative aluminum or steel articles the product of the United Kingdom, as provided for in subdivisions (c)(i)-(iv) and (d) of U.S. note 16 to this subchapter / Rates of duty (1-General): The duty provided in the applicable subheading + 25%" with expression_date 2026-07-31 and no effective date anywhere in the text. The 2026-07-21 basis is the HTS Rev 12 publication asserted in the commit message and the cross-review, not text in the cited provision (unlike the sibling repairs in this commit, which cite FR 2026-15181 and FR 2026-14542 DATES). The pre-fix 07-23 was equally ungrounded in the provision text, so this remains a date-versus-source correction rather than a policy choice. (2) The first reader's stated consequence — "leaving entries on 07-21 and 07-22 without the UK overlay" — is likely overstated: the predecessor module us/policies/usitc/us-tariff-duty/overlays/section-232-aluminum/uk-rate.yaml (HTS 9903.85.12) carries effective_from '2026-02-15' with no effective_to and the same 0.25 rate, so at module level the UK +25% was still expressible on 07-21/07-22; which heading actually fires is decided by the composition, which the PR says was "reworked accordingly". The classification rests on the window itself being wrong, not on a duty-amount gap.
